newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors seek arrest warrants for MPs.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors seek arrest warrants for MPs.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors said on Tuesday they were seeking arrest warrants for two ruling party members of parliament, including a close associate of President Kim Young-sam, over a loan scandal.

A prosecution official said the warrants were for the arrest of Hong In-gil, a senior official at the presidential Blue House until last year, and Chung Jae-chull on charges of taking money from the troubled Hanbo Group.

Hong was accused of taking 800 million won ($922,000) and Chung 100 million won from Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-woo, in connection with huge loans to the conglomerate's steelmaking unit. The tycoon has already been arrested on charges of fraud and other violations,
Hanbo Steel Co, flagship of South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate, piled up five trillion won in loans before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
The prosecutors on Monday summoned Hong and Chung to determine if they accepted kickbacks from Hanbo and pressured bankers into offering loans to the company.
The two are the first politicians to have been probed over loans to Hanbo Steel, South Korea's second largest steelmaker. ($ = 867.80 won)
